verses.text: Then Job answered:
"I've heard plenty of talk like this. You're all miserable comforters!
Will these empty words ever end? What keeps driving you to answer?
I could talk just like you if our places were reversed. I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.
But I'd use my words to strengthen you. I'd say something that could ease your pain.
When I speak, my grief doesn't ease. When I keep quiet, how does that help?
God, you've worn me out. You've left everyone around me desolate.
You've made me waste away, and that stands as a witness against me. My thin body rises up and testifies to my face.
In his anger he tears at me and hunts me down. He grinds his teeth at me. My enemy fixes his eyes on me.
They open their mouths wide against me, slap my cheek to humiliate me, and gather together against me.
God hands me over to the ungodly and throws me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at peace, and he shattered me. He grabbed me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. Then he set me up as his target.
His archers surround me. He strikes through my kidneys without mercy and spills my bile on the ground.
He breaks through me again and again, charging at me like a giant.
I've sewn sackcloth against my skin and humbled my strength in the dust.
My face is red from crying, and deep darkness hangs over my eyelids,
even though my hands have done no violence and my prayer is pure.
Earth, don't cover my blood. Let my cry find no place to rest.
Even now my witness is in heaven. The one who can speak for me is on high.
My friends mock me, and my eyes pour out tears to God.
If only someone would plead for a person before God, as one person pleads for a neighbor.
In just a few years I'll go down the road from which no one returns.
